terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Matched to the three-quarter view. Elevation solved to 30 degrees, 8 above the initial visual estimate of 22; distance is 1.6x the bounding radius. Aspect and scale deltas are inside threshold at this pose, so the residual IoU gap is real shape difference rather than framing.
referenceCamera.solveMethod: swept azimuth/elevation/distance against diagnose_render silhouette metrics

objectClass.notes: A polyhedron, not a lofted fuselage: every surface is a flat facet meeting its neighbours at a visible crease, so authored vertex geometry reproduces the subject EXACTLY rather than approximating it. Four materials carry the whole object - charcoal satin hull, tinted canopy, cyan emissive, matte orange vent. The cyan strips are inset into recessed panel channels, not decals on flat faces; that is geometry, not texture.

reasoning: Scores total 16/24 - solidly `complex`. The silhouette is heavily interrupted (fins, feather plates, wingtip pods) and there are many visible subparts, but the hierarchy is shallow and there are only four materials.
materialLayerCount is 1, not 3: this is the rare subject where the material count is genuinely low. Hull, canopy, emissive, vent - no wear, no grime, no layered finish.
occlusionRisk 1, the lowest of any subject so far: four views cover top, side, rear and three-quarter, leaving only the belly unseen.
Held at `complex` rather than `ultra-complex`: fidelity here depends on getting the facet silhouette and the emissive routing right, not on microstructure.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex depth is required because identity lives in the facet breaks, the emissive channel routing and the three-nozzle propulsion layout. A spec with one hull root would validate and reproduce a generic dart.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Every hull surface is a flat polygon meeting its neighbours at a hard crease; there are no smooth transitions anywhere on the craft.
A continuous cyan strip runs the full length of the mid-hull chine, nose to tail, inset into the panel channel.
A V-shaped emissive run wraps the underside of the nose, apex forward.
A large angular emissive loop traces the rear wing panel on each side, following the panel breaks rather than a smooth curve.
Each dorsal fin carries an emissive strip along its outer face, parallel to the swept leading edge.
Each nozzle recess is filled with horizontal emissive bars: five on the central, four on each outboard.
Three octagonal recesses in the tail - one large central, two smaller outboard in the wingtip pods.
Matte orange rectangular blocks sit in recessed sockets: two on the dorsal spine, one per side aft. They take shading, so they are not emissive.
Dark blue tinted canopy, faceted like the hull, reading opaque with a hard specular rather than transparent.
Layered swept plates fan aft from each wing trailing edge, four per side, each overlapping the one below.
Each wingtip pod carries a cyan emissive slot on its leading face.
White decals: arrow-in-triangle logo and "07" on the nose, "EXIS" wordmark and a second "07" on the mid-hull side.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: Underside hidden in all four views. RESOLVED: built as a flat faceted belly, constrained by the side profile. Inference, not observation.
Canopy interior hidden behind an opaque tint. RESOLVED: no cockpit modelled.
Rear feather plate count reads 3-4. RESOLVED: four per side, matching the three-quarter view.
Nozzle grille bar count reads 4-5. RESOLVED: five on the central nozzle, four on each outboard, matching the rear view.
Arrow logo internal geometry is below resolution. RESOLVED: reproduced as a chevron-in-triangle approximation and labelled as such.

definitionOfDone: From the three-quarter review viewpoint the model reads as the same craft: same arrowhead planform, same wedge side profile, same three-nozzle tail.
The hull is visibly faceted - hard creases everywhere, no smooth surfaces.
All four emissive runs are present and routed along panel breaks: chine, nose chevron, wing loop, fin edge.
Three nozzles with grille bars, twin fins, four feather plates per side, orange vents.
Materials read satin-metallic charcoal with a genuinely emissive cyan that stays bright on shadowed faces.

featureGroups.name: Faceted hull form and silhouette
qualityCriteria: Arrowhead planform: wedge nose, chine flare, wide delta, fanned tail.
Side profile is a shallow wedge, deepest at mid-body, flat underside.
Every surface flat-shaded with visible creases; no smooth normals anywhere.
Proportions length 1.00 : span 0.62 : height 0.26.
failureModes: smooth-shaded fuselage, which reads as a different design language
proportions drifting toward a generic dart

featureGroups.name: Cyan emissive channel routing
qualityCriteria: Chine strip runs unbroken nose to tail.
Nose chevron wraps the underside, apex forward.
Wing loop follows panel breaks with angular corners, never a smooth curve.
Strips are INSET into recessed channels, visible as grooves in three-quarter view.
Emissive stays at full brightness on faces turned away from the key light.

featureGroups.name: Three-nozzle tail

featureGroups.name: Satin hull against unlit-bright emissive

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

nextRequiredEvidence: Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

lights.role: Main studio key, high and to port, matching the reference highlight direction.
Cool fill from the shadow side so dark facets stay separable rather than crushing.
Back rim that catches the trailing edges and fin tips. A rim is correct HERE - this is a studio product render, not the painted diorama where a rim would have read as stylised edge lighting.
Low ambient floor. Kept low deliberately: facet separation depends on contrast.

Contact shadow and ground shadow on, with ambient occlusion in the nozzle recesses and the channel grooves. Without occlusion in those recesses the nozzles read as flat discs rather than sockets, and the emissive channels lose their inset depth.

shadowBehavior.note: Ambient occlusion in nozzle recesses and light channels is what sells them as cut into the hull rather than painted on it.

bloom.note: The reference has a visible halo around every emissive run; without bloom the strips read as flat cyan paint.

forbidden: smooth vertex normals on hull materials

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

Low ambient floor. Kept low deliberately: facet separation depends on contrast.

featureReviews.notes: The strongest match. Three nozzles in the reference's arrangement - one large central, two smaller outboard inside the wingtip pods - each an octagonal recess rather than a cylinder, with five grille bars centrally and four per outboard exactly as the rear view shows. Reached only after three real repairs: the housings were closed solids, the grille quads faced forward, and the central grille sat ahead of the tail cap.

Charcoal satin hull with the specular tracking each crease, tinted canopy with a clearcoat hard specular, cyan that stays at full brightness on faces turned away from the key, and orange vents that take shading with no emissive channel. Bloom strength tuned twice: 0.55 blew the runs into white tubes and lifted the hull to pale grey, 0.22 dropped them to hairlines, 0.34 holds.

Twin swept fins and four recessed orange vents are right. The canopy is the shortfall: it now reads as a distinct tinted panel after the spine was lowered through its run and the glazing lifted, but it is smaller and less prominent than the reference's, which dominates the forward spine.

The design language is right - every surface is a flat facet meeting its neighbours at a hard crease, arrowhead planform, wedge nose, chine rail the full length, and bilateral symmetry error 0.157. The faceting is COARSER than the reference: nine lofted stations give large panels where the reference subdivides the nose and forward hull into many smaller ones. Silhouette IoU 0.613 against a 0.85 threshold, with aspect and scale inside tolerance, so the gap is shape rather than framing.

Chine run, rear wing loop, fin strips and wingtip slots are present, angular, and inset into channels rather than painted on flat faces. Two shortfalls: the reference carries a large angular V on the FORWARD hull that is not modelled at all, and the nose chevron sits low enough that it only reads from underneath.

Four plates per side at the right sweep and stagger, and wingtip pods terminating each wing with an emissive slot. The plates read as flat shelves rather than the reference's stacked swept blades - each needs a tapered chord and a sharper trailing point.

reviewHistory.summary: Faceted hull authored as nine lofted cross-section stations with per-face normals, plus spine, canopy, twin fins, wingtip pods, four feather plates per side, recessed orange vents, the cyan channel network, generated canvas decals and the three-nozzle tail. Turntable gate passes first time (0 holes, 4/4 azimuths, reliable segmentation); part coverage passes with 0 errors. Reference camera solved by sweep to az 38 / el 30 / 1.6r, giving aspect delta 0.003 and scale delta 0.063 - both inside threshold - so silhouette IoU 0.613 is real shape difference. Two of five critical features pass.
corrections: An earlier draft of the faceted-hull note cited bilateralSymmetryError 0.157 as evidence of symmetry. That figure came from a different capture and the metric is meaningless on a three-quarter view (it reads 0.449 here). Corrected in place.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.

risks.description: Computed vertex normals would smooth the facets and destroy the entire design language.
risks.mitigation: flatShading on every hull material; faceted-hull review target is mustPass.

risks.description: Rendering the cyan as a bright lit colour instead of an emitter makes it dim on shadowed faces, which the reference never does.
risks.mitigation: emissive channel with intensity 2.6-3.4, checked on a face turned away from the key light.

risks.description: The orange vents are matte and shaded; treating them as a second accent light is the easy mistake.
risks.mitigation: vent-orange carries no emissive channel at all.
